plan.hypothesis: Overfitting control: apparent vs. adjusted Cox-Snell R² difference ≤ 0.05 (Nagelkerke scale) at 95% CI
assumptions: Anticipated adjusted Cox-Snell R² = 0.12 after internal validation/shrinkage
Shrinkage factor = 0.95 (98% of original apparent model performance retained)
Single-center or population cohort (standard Riley development scenario)
missing_information: Confirmation whether default pmsampsize 1.1.3 precision thresholds are acceptable, or if alternative shrinkage/performance targets are preferred
clarification_questions: Should the calculation proceed with pmsampsize 1.1.3 defaults for absolute precision on predicted outcome risk (±0.05 absolute margin of error on outcome probability scale)?
Is the anticipated adjusted Cox-Snell R² = 0.12 based on prior similar models, pilot data, or expert elicitation?
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2020) recommend sample size planning for prediction model development to balance adequate EPV (events per variable) with control of overfitting.
Shrinkage = 0.95 implies acceptable 5% relative performance loss from apparent to adjusted model, typical for rigorous internal validation.
Cox-Snell R² may be converted to Nagelkerke (adjusted) scale for intuitive interpretation on 0–1 range.
Precision criteria on average predicted risk addresses clinical utility: ability to reliably estimate outcome probability across the risk spectrum.
